newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees continuing low U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees continuing low U.S. inflation.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Friday he sees inflation staying low for the foreseeable future despite the recent low jobless rate.
He told reporters after a speech to the Bretton Woods Commission the U.S. always needed to be watchful about inflation picking up but that so far there was no sign of it re-igniting.
"Inflation most likely will remain low," Rubin said.

With the unemployment rate hovering at about a 7-1/2-year low, some analysts have voiced concern that tight labor markets will lead to wage-push inflation, but Rubin said he saw no sign of that happening.
"I don't see signs of inflation re-igniting," Rubin said.
The Labor Department said Thursday consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in October, the same amount as in September.
Excluding the often volatile food and energy sector, the core rate was more subdued, rising 0.2 percent after being up 0.3 percent in the prior month.
